title: The HAM10000 dataset, a large collection of multi-source dermatoscopic images of common pigmented skin lesions
authors: Philipp Tschandl, Cliff Rosendahl, Harald Kittler
venue: Scientific Data (Nature Publishing Group), vol. 5, article 180161
conclusions: Introduces the HAM10000 ("Human Against Machine with 10000 training images") dataset: 10015 dermatoscopic images of pigmented skin lesions collected over 20 years from two sites (Medical University of Vienna and Cliff Rosendahl's Queensland practice).

Unifies diverse historical image sources (PowerPoint slides, digitized diapositives, digital dermatoscopy systems) via an automated + manual curation pipeline, including a fine-tuned InceptionV3 classifier to filter dermatoscopic vs. close-up/overview images.
Defines seven generic diagnostic categories used as the benchmark classes: akiec, bcc, bkl, df, mel (melanoma), nv, and vasc, covering >95% of pigmented lesions seen in clinical practice.
Ground truth combines histopathology (>50% of lesions), follow-up examination, expert consensus, or confocal microscopy confirmation.
Released via the ISIC archive (CC BY-NC 4.0) to support both machine-learning benchmarking and human-vs-machine diagnostic comparison studies (used for the ISIC 2018 classification challenge).

Provides a comparison table showing HAM10000 is substantially larger and has higher pathologic verification than prior public dermatoscopic datasets (PH2, Atlas, ISIC 2017, and internal ViDIR/Rosendahl subsets).
